Doddily iPhone app waiting for Apple

Social playbook

Everything the account needs for its first two months: what to set up while Apple reviews the app, what to post on launch day, and a library of feed posts, Stories and Reels big enough to keep going without writing anything new.

Feed posts Stories 6 Reel scripts 4-week calendar

The idea

Every post answers the question parents ask each morning: what’s on for my little one today? Be the useful account first and the app second. People follow for the ideas, then download for the timetable.

Who we’re talking to

Parents and carers of babies and toddlers, often on parental leave, with a nap window and nothing planned. Grandparents, nannies and childminders too. Start local, in Hackney and north-east London, where you can check listings yourself and reply with real tips, then widen to other cities as posts prove what works.

How it should sound

Like a friend who always knows what’s on: warm, short, specific. Real days, times and walking distances beat adjectives. No “mama”, no guilt, nothing about “getting it right”. Everyone who looks after a small child is welcome, so write “parents and carers”.

The plan, in order

Launch day is the day Apple approves the app. Until then, build the account, but don’t link to the App Store or doddily.app.

1

Now, during review

Tonight to launch
  • Instagram @doddily.app is claimed. Do TikTok and Threads too
  • Profile photo: the flower on navy. Bio: “What’s on for your little one today. Coming soon to iPhone.”
  • Post teasers 1 to 3, one a day, and run the countdown Story
  • Record the screen videos for the Reels
2

Launch day

The day Apple approves
  • App Store link into every bio
  • Post the launch post and pin it
  • Reel 1 on Instagram and TikTok
  • Stories all day: the countdown ending, the app on your own phone, a thank you
  • Tell friends, family and your antenatal group yourself, in your own words
3

Weeks 1 to 4

Build the habit
  • Follow the calendar below: 3 posts, 1 Reel, Stories most days
  • Reply to every comment and DM with a real suggestion
  • Share in local Facebook parent groups where admins allow it
  • Note which posts get saved and shared
4

Week 5 onwards

Decide what’s next
  • Repeat the two post types with the most saves, drop the weakest
  • Add a second city if the London posts are working
  • Only then boost the best Reel, for example £5 a day for a week, London only

Four kinds of post

Roughly this mix. Most posts are useful even to someone who never downloads the app.

About half

What’s on

Round-ups by theme and area: free rhyme times, rainy-day soft play, weekend farms. Real days, times and places. These get saved.

About a quarter

How it works

One feature per post: search, Rainy day, children’s ages, the map, saving, calendar, directions.

About a fifth

The 9am problem

The shared moment: the nap ends and you need somewhere to be by 10. Relatable, never mocking, no photos of real children.

Now and then

Behind the app

Why it exists, no ads or account, where listings come from, and new features as they ship.

Four weeks, day by day

Post on weekday mornings between 7 and 9, while parents plan the day. Batch each week on Sunday evening. Numbers refer to the posts below.

Feed posts

All 4:5 (1080 × 1350), the tallest Instagram allows, so they fill more of the screen. Carousels are 4:5 too — swipe the artwork to see each slide. “Copy caption” copies the caption and hashtags together.

Stories

9:16 (1080 × 1920). Stickers are what make Stories work: a poll or a question doubles the replies, and every reply tells Instagram to show your next post to more people. Each card says which sticker to add.

Reels and TikToks

Screen recordings of the app with big on-screen text, no voice needed. Record on your phone once it’s live, or on the simulator before then. Keep each under 20 seconds and end on the app’s name.

House rules

  • No photos, names or stories of your own family. Use the app, the flower and type.
  • Only post what the app really does. No invented reviews, ratings or download numbers.
  • Talk about providers kindly, and never imply a partnership that doesn’t exist. Tagging a class you love is fine.
  • No links to the App Store or doddily.app until Apple approves the app.
  • In parent groups, read the rules first, ask an admin when unsure, help first and mention the app second.
  • When a listing is wrong, thank the person and fix it. Point people to hello@doddily.app.
  • Reply to every comment and DM in the first hour if you can. Early replies are what spread a post.

Ticks are saved in this browser only.

What to watch

Check once a week, when you plan the next one. Followers matter less than saves and shares.

Saves and sharesThe clearest sign a post was useful. Make more of whatever gets them.
Story repliesPolls and questions that get answered tell Instagram to show the next post wider.
Profile link tapsUnder Insights. The step before a download.
App Store page viewsIn App Store Connect, under Analytics, next to downloads.
